meta.phase-name: Gameplay Responsiveness And Content-Driven Board UX

phase-plan.purpose: Return the active development lane to the playable game. Improve responsiveness, room/entity readability, hover media, and board clarity while preserving the now-usable local authoring/import/publish path as a supporting tool rather than the current center of gravity.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: a dedicated turn-runner seam between KAPLAY UI and engine dispatch, off-main-thread or worker-ready execution for expensive turn resolution, explicit busy/pending state in the UI, stronger room identity and entity visibility on the navigation board, content-driven hover cards/media for rooms/hostiles/dungeoneers, and Playwright coverage for the core playable loop. Also in scope: updating gameplay-facing planning references so design and implementation stay aligned during the human feedback loop. Out of scope: broad new editor productization, generalized planner work in docs-site, and content-pipeline polish that does not directly improve playing or iterating on the game right now.

file.description: Current scene/runtime bootstrap and main-thread action execution. This is the first place to insert a dedicated turn runner and pending-turn UI state.
Bridge between KAPLAY and the engine package. It should stop being a direct synchronous dispatch surface and become the deterministic execution boundary for workerized or queued turn computation.
Main gameplay scene orchestration. It should consume pending-turn state, improve board readability, and stop embedding heavy turn work directly in input handlers.
Board rendering and retained decoration update path. This is the right place to improve room/entity marker readability without bloating the orchestration file again.
Derived room visuals/cache keys. Use this layer to keep content-driven room identity and board diffing cheap.
Deterministic synchronous rules engine. Keep the game logic deterministic here even if execution moves behind a worker or queued turn runner on the UI side.
Playwright smoke coverage for the playable game loop should grow here so gameplay regressions are visible without manual spelunking.
Primary gameplay design reference that should stay aligned with the room board, encounters, visibility, and content-authored presentation improvements.

task.description: Introduce a dedicated turn-runner seam in KAPLAY so gameplay input no longer assumes same-tick synchronous engine mutation. Keep the engine deterministic, but move the UI toward queued/background turn execution with explicit pending-state handling.

Improve room/entity readability on the board and HUD: stronger room identity, clearer hostile/dungeoneer presence, better same-room encounter emphasis, and hover/preview detail that makes location and occupancy obvious.
Bind the first content-driven media/icon previews into room/entity hover cards so authored content can drive the board language instead of placeholder text alone.
Add Playwright game smoke coverage for the navigation loop, room preview/selection, encounter visibility, and busy-turn behavior so the feedback loop stays fast and reviewable.

decision.summary: Off-main-thread execution should not make the core engine semantically async. The engine remains deterministic and synchronous internally; the UI/runtime boundary becomes asynchronous.
decision.impact: This protects reproducibility, keeps tests simpler, and lets workerization improve responsiveness without rewriting gameplay rules around promises.

decision.summary: The active lane is gameplay-first again. Asset Explorer and local authoring remain supporting tools, but they are no longer allowed to eclipse readable, responsive play.
decision.impact: Implementation order now follows the human feedback loop in the game itself: play, observe, adjust, then return to content authoring when that loop needs better data/tools.
